scenes.title: UPDATE
scenes.narration: UPDATE changes values in existing rows, and its WHERE clause decides which rows are affected.

scenes.title: Changing data
scenes.narration: UPDATE uses SET to assign new values to one or more columns. The WHERE clause is critical because it restricts the change to matching rows. Leaving WHERE off updates every row in the table, which is rarely what you want.

scenes.title: Updating selected rows
scenes.narration: This statement raises prices by ten percent for a specific category. SET computes the new price from the existing one for each affected row. The WHERE clause ensures only products in the Books category are changed.

scenes.title: How an update runs
scenes.narration: The database first locates the rows that satisfy the WHERE condition. It then applies the SET assignments to each of those rows and writes the new values. Rows that do not match are left completely unchanged.

scenes.text: Never forget the WHERE clause in an UPDATE, or you may change far more rows than intended.
scenes.narration: Always double-check the WHERE clause before running an UPDATE, since forgetting it will silently rewrite every row in the table.
